wiki_text: As of 2025, Mediterranean Gas (MedGas) targets July 2027 commercial operation for the Argo FSRU at the port of Volos. DESFA accepted a capacity-reservation technical form (10-04-2025) for the 'ARGO' new entry point: 131,833 MWh/day baseload (4.6 BCM/y), with a limited-period maximum of 5.2 BCM/y. The FSRU vessel is to be leased through BW LNG, with Lithuania's Klaipedos Nafta expected to act as terminal operator; ExxonMobil LNG is expected to supply cargoes (US/Qatar sources). Romania's state TSO Transgaz reported (Sept 2023) an agreement to acquire a 15% stake. Market test demand exceeded total capacity, with commitments spanning up to 25 years. The terminal aims to supply North Macedonia, Bulgaria, Romania, Albania and Italy in addition to Greece.

In May 2026, Mercuria and Motor Oil Hellas signed a memorandum of understanding covering (1) regasification capacity reservation at the Dioriga Gas FSRU, (2) long-term LNG supply from Mercuria for delivery through the terminal, and (3) joint development toward commercial operation. The project is described as 'the most advanced and mature FSRU project in Greece,' bringing 21-24 TWh of LNG imports (about 30% of the Greek market) and 177,000 cbm of additional storage in southern Greece. An earlier standoff in which DESFA moved to exclude the project from its 2026-2035 development plan (citing unmet contractual obligations) was resolved, returning Dioriga to the necessary-infrastructure list. As of May 2026 the developer was obtaining a sea license and a third-party-access exemption from RAAEY and negotiating with LNG market participants. FID remained pending.

Greece signed the environmental permitting decision for Gastrade's second FSRU (Thrace, in the Alexandroupolis area) on 27 January 2026. The facility is planned for ~6 bcm/y of natural gas (comparable to the operating Alexandroupolis FSRU's ~5.5 bcm) and could enter service in 2028. A final investment decision could be taken by Q1 2027, contingent on securing new 15-year LNG supply agreements. Estimated cost is at least EUR 650 million - higher than the first Alexandroupolis FSRU - and, unlike the first project, it has no access to European Investment Bank subsidies or preferential financing, so advancement hinges on commercial viability.

topic: HELLENiQ sole ownership, FSU addition, and 2029 timeline
wiki_text: HELLENiQ ENERGY completed its acquisition of the remaining 50% of Elpedison B.V. on 15 July 2025 (EUR 164m plus ~EUR 19m for cash reserves), buying out EDF group's Edison and becoming Elpedison's sole shareholder after a 15-year joint venture; Elpedison was subsequently rebranded 'Enerwave' (launched 12 November 2025). Elpedison/Enerwave now targets commercial operation of the Thessaloniki FSRU by January 2029 (originally 2025), with environmental licensing expected by April 2026 followed by market testing. The regulator RAAEY approved enhancing the project with a second floating unit, so the design comprises an FSRU plus a Floating Storage Unit (FSU) connected via a 4.5 km subsea and 7 km onshore pipeline section. Stated entry capacity is up to 150,000 MWh/day (about 7.3 bcm/y). It would be Greece's third LNG facility after Revithoussa and Alexandroupolis.
